 Scary weather: Torrential Halloween rain prompts flood warning
 The National Weather Services has issued a flash flood warning for parts of the Las Vegas Valley Saturday night.
 Lightning streaks through the sky during the Halloween Safe Night on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, at the Doolittle Community Center in Las Vegas. (Liv Paggiarino/Las Vegas Review-Journal) Kids in costume line up to get candy against stormy skies during the Halloween Safe Night on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, at the Doolittle Community Center in Las Vegas. (Liv Paggiarino/Las Vegas Review-Journal) A ghost balloon waves in the wind during the Halloween Safe Night on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, at the Doolittle Community Center in Las Vegas. (Liv Paggiarino/Las Vegas Review-Journal) Rain is seen falling in the Centennial Hills area on Oct. 31, 2026. (Traci Wilson/Las Vegas Review-Journal) Lightning streaks through the sky during the Halloween Safe Night on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, at the Doolittle Community Center in Las Vegas. (Liv Paggiarino/Las Vegas Review-Journal) More Stories 1 dead in Henderson after heavy rain triggers three water rescue operations Rain on Halloween? 38-year dry streak likely to end — but Las Vegas trick-or-treaters shouldn’t fret More October storms dump rain on parts of Las Vegas area — PHOTOS Golf ball-sized hail pound parts of Arizona — PHOTOS 
 By Amanda Meagher and Brett Clarkson 
 / 
 Las Vegas Review-Journal 
 October 31, 2026 - 6:55 pm 
 Updated October 31, 2026 - 8:17 pm 
 Saturday night’s weather felt more like a cruel trick, no treat, as the skies above the Las Vegas Valley opened up and dumped buckets of rain on parts of the area just in time for Halloween night.
 The wet weather had the all-too-serious potential to be the scariest part of Saturday’s culmination of spooky season. The National Weather Service’s Las Vegas forecast office issued a flash flood warning Saturday night that was in effect until about 9:15 p.m. It was then extended until 9:45 p.m.
 Among the potential hazards, the weather service said: life-threatening flash flooding.
 “At 621 PM PDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area,” the weather service’s Las Vegas forecast office posted on its website. “Between 0.25 and 0.75 inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.”
 The warning applied to Las Vegas, North Las Vegas, Lone Mountain, Centennial Hills, Aliante, Summerlin, North Las Vegas Airport and Floyd Lamb Park, the weather service said.
 At about 7:45 p.m., between a quarter-inch and a half-inch of rain had fallen, the weather service said. The worst of it may have been over, but the flood risk still remained, forecasters said.
 “Although the heaviest rainfall has ended, additional flooding due to runoff remains possible,” the weather service said.
 In neighborhoods throughout the valley, trick-or-treaters brave enough to face the elements were seen hoisting umbrellas as they went door to door. Some trudged on as lightning streaked the sky.
 Saturday’s weather followed Friday’s deluge of heavy rain and hail in parts of the valley.
 In Henderson on Friday, a person who was rescued from a wash by firefighters near Lake Mead Parkway went into cardiac arrest and died, a Henderson city spokesperson said in an email.
 Two people were also rescued from a vehicle swept off the road by floodwaters near Lake Mead Parkway east of the Lake Las Vegas entrance and another person was rescued from the top of a vehicle trapped in floodwaters near North Milan Street and Drake Street, the email said. There were no injuries reported.
 Parts of the valley saw over 1.5 inches of rain on Friday, according to county rain gauge data. Downtown Las Vegas saw over an inch by Friday afternoon.
 This is a developing story. Check back for updates.
